This notebook relies heavily on: 

1. [Analyzing RNA-seq data with DESeq2](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html)

2. [RNA-Seq workflow: gene-level exploratory analysis and differential expression](https://f1000research.com/articles/4-1070/v2)

3. [Beginner’s guide to using the DESeq2 package](https://bioc.ism.ac.jp/packages/2.14/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/beginner.pdf)

4. [Count Regression](https://stats4nr.com/count-regression)

5. [Exploring DESeq2 results: Wald test](https://hbctraining.github.io/DGE_workshop_salmon_online/lessons/05b_wald_test_results.html)



## Strategy

1. Load Master Data set

2. Load Individual Sample Data Sets

3. For each VHH in the sample sets
  * Locate in master set, and assign clone id

4. Proceed with DESeq2

## Real Data

  clone_count <- length(unique(files[[nm]]$clone_id))

    files[[nm]]$VHH <- fixed_translate_DNA(files[[nm]]$sequence_alignment)

    files[[nm]]$VHH <- substr(files[[nm]]$VHH, 11, nchar(files[[nm]]$VHH))
    files[[nm]] <- unproductive(files[[nm]])
  }
  
  print("After-Cleaning:")
  print(length(unique(files[[nm]]$clone_id)))
  print(sum(files[[nm]]$duplicate_count))
  cat('\n')
  
  if (max_clone_count < clone_count){
    max_clone_count <- clone_count
    max_id <- nm
  }
}

## First Step: Assign Identical Clonal Families across Experiments

We'll do this with `junction_aa` for now, then we will use `VHH` later?

```{r}
res <- data.frame()

for (f in names(files)[names(files) != "master"]){
  # Subset data frame
  tmp <- files[[f]]
  print(f)
  #print(table(tmp$clone_id))
  # Iterate over each VHH
  count <- 0
  max_count <- length(unique(tmp$junction_aa))
  for (CDR3 in unique(tmp$junction_aa)){
    count <- count + 1
    if (round(count/max_count*100, 2) %% 5 == 0) cat("Progress:", round(count/max_count*100, 2), '\n')
    tmp_frame <- tmp[tmp$junction_aa == CDR3,]
    tmp_frame$clone_id <- rep(master[which(master$junction_aa == CDR3),]$clone_id[1], nrow(tmp_frame))
    tmp_frame$f <- rep(f, nrow(tmp_frame))
    # Rbind those
    res <- rbind(res, tmp_frame)
  }
}
```

results <- tmp[,c(1:2)]

for (nm in colnames(tmp)[3:ncol(tmp)]){
  # Subset the columns we need
  tmp_frame <- tmp[,c("median_CDR3", nm)]
  # Order and add rank statistic
  tmp_frame <- tmp_frame[order(tmp_frame[[nm]], decreasing = TRUE),]
  tmp_frame[[paste0(nm, '.rank')]] <- 1:nrow(tmp_frame)
  # Merge on median_CDR3 
  results <- merge(results, tmp_frame, by = "median_CDR3")
}

# Order according to dendrogram


```{r}
dat <- read.csv("~/VHH/data/Cluster-DBs/phylogenetic_dbs/translated_dbs/culled_databases/GS_d2_18Jun24-Cleaned19Apr24.csv", header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)

clonal_statistics <- function(dat){
  # Hold results in results
  results <- data.frame()
  # Iterate over clone ids
  for (nm in unique(dat$clone_id)){
    tmp_frame <- dat[dat$clone_id == nm,]
    # Unroll
    unrolled_VHHs <- unroll_dupes_fast(tmp_frame, "VHH")
    unrolled_CDR3s <- unroll_dupes_fast(tmp_frame, "junction_aa")
    # Pull statistics
    median_VHH <- names(table(unrolled_VHHs)[order(table(unrolled_VHHs), decreasing = T)][1])
    median_CDR3 <- names(table(unrolled_CDR3s)[order(table(unrolled_CDR3s), decreasing = T)][1])
    abundance <- sum(tmp_frame$duplicate_count)
    
    # Keep the integer as the cluster_id
    clone_id <- nm
    
    results <- rbind(results, cbind(clone_id, median_CDR3, median_VHH, abundance))
  }
  return(results)
}

dat <- clonal_statistics(dat)
```

Merge data

```{r}
test <- merge(tmp, dat[,c("median_CDR3", "median_VHH")], by = c("median_CDR3"))

# Drop ranks
test <- test[,!grepl("rank", colnames(test))]
test$overall <- rowSums(test[,c(2:5)])
```



```{r}
strings <- test$median_VHH

CDR3s <- test$median_CDR3

# Compute the distance matrix using
dist_matrix <- stringdistmatrix(strings, method = "lv")

# Perform hierarchical clustering

counts <- 1

main_title <- paste("Cluster Dendrogram of CDR3 families from Abundance Data\nDemand >= ", counts," VHHs, Distance Metric: Levenshtein", sep = '')

# test <- test[cluster_tree$order,]
```

```{r}

## Load Global Set

To do this, since we only have clonal family data, we need VHHs

```{r}
dat <- read.csv("~/VHH/data/Cluster-DBs/phylogenetic_dbs/translated_dbs/culled_databases/GS_d2_18Jun24-Cleaned19Apr24.csv", header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)

clonal_statistics <- function(dat){
  # Hold results in results
  results <- data.frame()
  # Iterate over clone ids
  for (nm in unique(dat$clone_id)){
    tmp_frame <- dat[dat$clone_id == nm,]
    # Unroll
    unrolled_VHHs <- unroll_dupes_fast(tmp_frame, "VHH")
    unrolled_CDR3s <- unroll_dupes_fast(tmp_frame, "junction_aa")
    # Pull statistics
    median_VHH <- names(table(unrolled_VHHs)[order(table(unrolled_VHHs), decreasing = T)][1])
    median_CDR3 <- names(table(unrolled_CDR3s)[order(table(unrolled_CDR3s), decreasing = T)][1])
    abundance <- sum(tmp_frame$duplicate_count)
    
    # Keep the integer as the cluster_id
    clone_id <- nm
    
    results <- rbind(results, cbind(clone_id, median_CDR3, median_VHH, abundance))
  }
  return(results)
}

tmp <- clonal_statistics(dat)
```

### Create XLSX file

```{r}
# Install and load the openxlsx package
install.packages("openxlsx")
library(openxlsx)

# Create a sample data frame
df <- data.frame(
  Name = c("John", "Jane", "Doe"),
  Age = c(23, 25, 28),
  Score = c(85, 90, 88)
)

# Create a workbook and add a worksheet
wb <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(wb, "Sheet1")

# Write the data frame to the worksheet
writeData(wb, "Sheet1", df)

# Create a custom style with Courier font
courier_style <- createStyle(fontName = "Courier New")

# Apply the style to the entire worksheet
addStyle(wb, "Sheet1", style = courier_style, rows = 1:nrow(df) + 1, cols = 1:ncol(df), gridExpand = TRUE)

# Save the workbook
saveWorkbook(wb, "data.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)

```

  # Repeat the median_CDR3 value according to the abundance and create a data frame
  expanded_row <- data.frame(
    median_CDR3 = rep(cdr3, times = abundance),
    abundance = rep(1, times = abundance) # We set abundance to 1 in each repetition
  )
  
  # Combine the expanded row with the existing expanded data frame
  expanded_df <- rbind(expanded_df, expanded_row)
}

# Reset row names
rownames(expanded_df) <- NULL

```{r}
clonal_statistics <- function(dat){
  # Hold results in results
  results <- data.frame()
  # Iterate over clone ids
  count <- 0
  for (nm in unique(dat$clone_id)){
    if (!is.na(nm)){
        tmp_frame <- dat[which(dat$clone_id == as.character(nm)),]
       # cat("[Clonal Statistics] Clone ID:", nm, '\n')
        # 
      #  cat("Indices with NA's introduced:")
       # print(which(is.na(tmp_frame$duplicate_count)))
      #  cat("Dropping NAs\n")
        # Unroll
        # unrolled_VHHs <- unroll_dupes_fast(tmp_frame, "VHH")
        unrolled_CDR3s <- unroll_dupes_fast(tmp_frame, "junction_aa")
        # Pull statistics
        # median_VHH <- names(table(unrolled_VHHs)[order(table(unrolled_VHHs), decreasing = T)][1])
        median_CDR3 <- names(table(unrolled_CDR3s)[order(table(unrolled_CDR3s), decreasing = T)][1])
        abundance <- sum(tmp_frame$duplicate_count)
        
        # Keep the integer as the cluster_id
        clone_id <- nm
        
        results <- rbind(results, cbind(clone_id, median_CDR3, abundance))
    } else {
      cat('NA\n')
      count <- count + 1
    }
  }
  cat("There were: ", count, "NA values in the data for some reason.\n")
  return(results)
}

unroll_dupes_fast <- function(dat, unroll_column) {
  # Repeat each element of the unroll column based on duplicate count
  result_vec <- rep(dat[[unroll_column]], times = dat$duplicate_count)
  return(result_vec)
}

## Create Cluster Dendrogram

We need to load VHH data

```{r}

```{r}


dat <- read.csv("~/VHH/data/Cluster-DBs/phylogenetic_dbs/translated_dbs/culled_databases/GS_d2_18Jun24-Cleaned19Apr24.csv", header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)

clonal_statistics <- function(dat){
  # Hold results in results
  results <- data.frame()
  # Iterate over clone ids
  for (nm in unique(dat$clone_id)){
    tmp_frame <- dat[dat$clone_id == nm,]
    # Unroll
    unrolled_VHHs <- unroll_dupes_fast(tmp_frame, "VHH")
    unrolled_CDR3s <- unroll_dupes_fast(tmp_frame, "junction_aa")
    # Pull statistics
    median_VHH <- names(table(unrolled_VHHs)[order(table(unrolled_VHHs), decreasing = T)][1])
    median_CDR3 <- names(table(unrolled_CDR3s)[order(table(unrolled_CDR3s), decreasing = T)][1])
    abundance <- sum(tmp_frame$duplicate_count)
    
    # Keep the integer as the cluster_id
    clone_id <- nm
    
    results <- rbind(results, cbind(clone_id, median_CDR3, median_VHH, abundance))
  }
  return(results)
}

tmp <- clonal_statistics(dat)

## Add ranks

```{r}
# Drop the abundance relic that we got from clonal_statistics
tmp$abundance <- NULL

# We will begin with the first set of abundances
results <- tmp[,c(1:4)]
# Order and add ranks
results <- results[order(results[,4], decreasing = TRUE),]
results[[paste0(colnames(results)[4], '.rank')]] <- 1:nrow(results)

# Iterate over all columns after first
for (nm in colnames(tmp)[5:ncol(tmp)]){
  # Subset the columns we need
  tmp_frame <- tmp[,c("median_CDR3", nm)]
  # Order and add rank statistic
  tmp_frame <- tmp_frame[order(tmp_frame[[nm]], decreasing = TRUE),]
  tmp_frame[[paste0(nm, '.rank')]] <- 1:nrow(tmp_frame)
  # Merge on median_CDR3 
  results <- merge(results, tmp_frame, by = "median_CDR3")
}
